Here’s the main idea in tutor-friendly terms:

- **Perfect separation (no mistakes allowed):** It assumes the two classes are **linearly separable**, meaning you can draw a boundary (a line in 2D, a plane in 3D, etc.) that puts all points of one class on one side and all points of the other class on the other side.

- **Maximize the margin:** Among all the hyperplanes that separate the classes, it chooses the one with the **largest margin**—the biggest “gap” between the boundary and the closest data points from either class. Intuition: a bigger margin tends to generalize better because the decision boundary is less sensitive to small shifts/noise.

- **Support vectors define the boundary:** Only the points **closest to the hyperplane** (the ones “touching” the margin) matter for the final solution. Those are the **support vectors**; moving other points (as long as they stay on the correct side) doesn’t change the classifier.
